source_acquisition.search_note: The official proceedings PDF is the fact source for the 31-page object inventory, labels, captions, page placement and final layout. The source-inventory row reports no_public_source_found and corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-eb4983c11917/ has no acquired local visual source. gh verified the author project repository/tree and its LSBS page; the tree contains display PNGs and the paper PDF but no committed plotting scripts, result data or final proceedings TeX. Direct arXiv source 2509.26625 supplies paper.tex, fairmeta.cls, table TeX and visual PDF assets that map to Figures 2–14. Figure 1 is absent from that source, and the arXiv/project rendering is 33 pages with several caption/layout differences from the 31-page target proceedings PDF. The direct assets therefore support a partial_visual_source classification, not exact_visual_source; no weights, checkpoints or datasets were fetched.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Charts use bright yellow–green–blue/purple categorical or sequential palettes; line series are often differentiated by color plus markers, while Figure 7 adds a 100% reference line. Qualitative panels use pale yellow/green/blue cards and ✓/✗ text. Tables are monochrome booktabs layouts with group headers and sparse bold emphasis.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The proceedings page, captions and table rules are PDF text/vector objects. Imported chart assets combine vector axes/text with raster or embedded plot surfaces; qualitative panels combine raster imagery and vector/text cards. The complete target PDF was rendered at 200 dpi, with targeted object pages inspected at high detail.
paper_style.style_consistency: The single-column proceedings frame and serif body/table typography are stable across main text and appendix. Figures share a small-multiple chart grammar and table objects share grouped headers/precision conventions. Qualitative panels are structurally consistent, but chart palettes, undefined translucent bands, and small imported labels reduce cross-object and grayscale consistency.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Impact of model and data sizes. The plots illustrate the performance of MLLMs, built upon LLMs of five different sizes (340M to 13B parameters), as a function of the amount of web-crawl pre-training data (0B to 100B tokens). The general trend shows that performance improves with both increasing model size and data volume, but the scaling behavior differs across task categories.

figures.data_and_statistics: Five model sizes (340M–13B) are evaluated at eight web-crawl data volumes from 0B to 100B. Curves and visible translucent bands are rendered; the PDF does not define the band statistic, repetitions, denominator, or seed aggregation.
figures.evidence_relation: §3.1 scale intervention → Figure 2 的 category-specific dose response → Figure 3/4 分离 source 与 category proportion → Table 3 的大规模 recipe 验证。

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Performance of MLLMs on the Multi-Level Existence Bench (MLE-Bench). The left plot shows the overall accuracy for models pre-trained on 16 different single-source data types. Other plots detail performance on objects of varying relative sizes, from small (0-30% of image pixels) to medium (30-60%) to large (60-100%). The results demonstrate that pre-training on the broad and diverse web-crawl corpus is most effective in gaining perception prior, with its advantage being particularly pronounced for perceiving smaller objects.

figures.label: Figure 14

caption.text: Figure 14: Qualitative impact of visual world data on complex visual perception. The figure displays answers from five models—pre-trained with 0% to 100% visual combination data—to a question requiring an understanding of color constancy. The results show that while the model with 25% visual data provides the correct answer with reasoning relevant to the core visual principle, models trained on more visual data offer incorrect answers and flawed explanations. This suggests that simply increasing descriptive visual text does not necessarily cultivate a deeper perceptual understanding.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Grid Search for a vision-favorable data mixture. Results from pre-training a 3B parameter LLM on 30 distinct data blends, each totaling 30B tokens. The table explores how varying the proportions of reasoning-centric (rea) and visual-world (vis) data affects various capabilities.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty channel; every Avg VQA value is a single point estimate.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirty visible blend rows are split into two side-by-side blocks, each totaling 30B tokens on a 3B LLM. reasoning and visual ratios are integer percentages; Avg VQA is one decimal. The 60/15 value 32.7 is bold. The prose describes a 24-blend search although the PDF table/caption display 30 rows.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 4 proportion curves → Table 1 local grid search → Table 2 source-level interpolation and mix6 → Table 3 scale-up recipe.
design_strengths: Side-by-side blocks fit 30 rows in a narrow single-column float.
Two-level header and bold peak make the selected ratio visible.
Booktabs rules are print-friendly.
design_weaknesses: Wraptable placement competes with adjacent prose.
Left/right blocks repeat headers but have a weak group boundary.
Caption/prose count mismatch (30 versus 24) affects reproducibility.
tables.reusable_pattern: For a bounded grid, use symmetric blocks with fixed ratio/score headers and publish one consistent candidate count.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Deriving a data mixture for more vision-aware LLMs. This table details a series of 11 data mixtures, from mix0 (language-favorable blend) to mix10 (approximating the vision-favorable blend), all trained on a 3B-parameter LLM with 50B tokens. The results highlight a trade-off, with mix6 emerging as the most balanced mixture, achieving top-ranked overall performance by improving visual capabilities without a significant drop in language proficiency.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty channel; recipe metrics and rank are point estimates.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows mix0–mix10 span 14 columns: Recipe, vertical language/vision direction, 8 data-source mixture columns, t-acc, ppl, v-acc and Overall Rank. Mixture/accuracy values use one decimal, ppl two decimals, rank integer. Bold cells mark language baseline metrics, mix6 rank 1 and mix10 v-acc 33.4.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 1 ratio target → Table 2 language-to-vision recipe path → Table 3 Language-Favorable/Balanced validation.
design_strengths: One decision surface joins recipe proportions, language cost, visual gain and rank.
Direction arrows and vertical recipe marker preserve the trade-off.
design_weaknesses: Fourteen columns require small type and horizontal scanning.
Rank aggregation and tie handling are not defined in the table.
Bold emphasis is not accompanied by a caption-wide best-cell convention.
tables.reusable_pattern: Place recipe composition and modality metrics under a stable two-level header, with a published rule for rank construction.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Performance comparisons of the Language-Favorable and Balanced models across both language and vision-language benchmarks. The table summarizes key language metrics (perplexity and accuracy) and provides average scores for a suite of vision tasks.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty channel; each 7B/1T recipe row is a point estimate.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two recipe rows and eight columns compare language ppl/avg acc with five vision fields (General, Knowledge, OCR&Chart QA, Vision-Centric, Overall). ppl has two decimals, avg acc three, vision scores two; vertical separators divide Model/Language/Vision.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 2 mix0/mix6 choice → Table 3 minimal language–vision decision table → §4.2 and Table 6 blind-tuning increment.
design_strengths: Compact modality grouping makes the final trade-off easy to scan.
Precision and column labels are consistent with Table 2.
design_weaknesses: Two point-estimate rows give no stability information.
Five vision columns are small in a single-column float.
7B/1T construction conditions depend on surrounding prose.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a two-level Language/Vision header for the final recipe comparison and place scale plus uncertainty protocol in the caption.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Conceptual categories of key pre-training data corpus (%). The table shows the percentage of text segments from each data corpus classified into one of the conceptual categories.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, rank or failure channel; percentages are classification proportions.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six source rows and nine columns contain four reasoning and four visual category percentages plus Data sources. Values use one decimal. The multi-label classifier means category columns can overlap and need not sum to 100%.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix F 32B LLM multi-label classification → Table 4 source composition → Figures 3–4 and Table 2 mixture interpretation.
design_strengths: Symmetric reasoning/visual group headers make source profiles easy to compare.
One decimal is adequate for these proportions.
design_weaknesses: Nine narrow columns invite label wrapping.
A reader can mistake overlapping multi-label percentages for mutually exclusive bins.
Prompt and label reliability are outside the table.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use symmetric group headers for overlapping categories and state denominator, overlap and classifier conditions in the caption.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Model performance on the MLE-Bench. Results are reported in three splits based on object size in percentage (0-30, 30-60, 60-100), along with a weighted overall accuracy, evaluating the ability of different models to identify objects of varying sizes.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty channel; accuracy and weighted Overall are point estimates.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four external model rows and five columns report 0–30, 30–60, 60–100 and weighted Overall accuracy. Values use two decimals. Models are gpt-5, gpt-4o-mini, gemini-2.5-flash and claude-opus-4-20250514.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 12 benchmark interface → Table 5 external-model scale diagnostics → Appendix J interpretation of gpt-5, Gemini and Claude trade-offs.
design_strengths: Short header exposes each object-size slice and aggregate.
Two-decimal values support close model comparison.
design_weaknesses: No visual highlight for best/worst cells.
Overall weights and split counts are not in the table.
Inference settings and model versions rely on prose.
tables.reusable_pattern: Retain structural splits alongside a weighted aggregate, while publishing split denominators, weights and inference conditions.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Performance comparisons of the Lang-Favorable and Balanced models across both language and vision-language benchmarks with blind visual instruction tuning trick. The table summarizes key language metrics (perplexity and accuracy) and provides average scores for a suite of vision tasks, categorized as General, Knowledge, OCR & Chart QA, and Vision-Centric. It also shows the impact of applying our blind visual instruction tuning trick (+Blind). The blind tuning method provides an additional performance boost for both models.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty channel; +Blind rows are point estimates and leave language cells blank.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four rows compare Lang-Favorable/Balanced recipes with and without blind tuning across eight columns: Model, language ppl/avg acc, and five vision metrics. ppl uses two decimals, avg acc three, vision scores two. +Blind rows leave language cells empty because only visual tuning changes are reported.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 3 baseline recipes → Table 6 blind stage shows Knowledge gain and OCR drop → Appendix K/L explains shortcut and hallucination risk.
design_strengths: Paired ordinary/+Blind rows make the increment visible.
Modality grouping and precision match Table 3.
design_weaknesses: Blank language cells can be read as missing rather than not-applicable.
Caption emphasizes additional boost without highlighting OCR decline.
No hallucination rate or uncertainty accompanies the shortcut result.
tables.reusable_pattern: For an added training stage, pair baseline and variant rows under the same columns, use an explicit em dash for inapplicable cells, and show benefit plus side effect.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 defines four VQA channels; Figures 2–4 isolate scale, source and proportion; Tables 1–2 choose a calibrated mixture; Figure 5 diagnoses perception/reasoning clusters; Figures 6–7 test encoder and instruction-tuning boundaries; Table 3 closes the main recipe comparison. Appendix Figures 8–14 and Tables 4–6 expand object-scale evaluation, data classification, judge/alignment diagnostics, blind tuning and qualitative failure cases.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions start with bold descriptive titles and usually specify the intervention and comparison. Main findings are often repeated in captions for Figures 2, 3, 5, 6, 8–11 and Tables 2/6, while statistical definitions remain sparse. Figure 2/4 bands are visible without a caption definition; Figure 12 retains the PDF typo 60-90; Table 2 rank and Table 5 weighted Overall are not fully operationalized.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Result tables use modality/recipe or data-source group headers, metric direction arrows where applicable, consistent decimal precision, and booktabs/partial separators. Table 1 uses two repeated ratio blocks; Table 2 uses recipe-direction and mixture groups; Tables 3/6 use Language/Vision groups; Tables 4/5 use direct category/split columns.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The method claim about visual priors is operationalized by source/scale/proportion curves, then checked with correlation, encoder substitution and visual-instruction removal. Tables 1–3 convert those trends into a recipe, while Appendix qualitative panels and Table 6 expose shortcut and failure boundaries.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The main body keeps the scale/source/mixture chain and final 1T comparison. Appendix F/G supplies data and instruction classification, I/J supplies MLE construction/results, A supplies judge/alignment hypotheses, K/L/M supplies blind-tuning risks and qualitative cases. Figure 12 caption inconsistency is resolved in favor of the PDF visual row plus Table 5/appendix text (60-100) for interpretation, while the literal caption is preserved above.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern-like math dominate page text, captions and tables. Imported chart labels are smaller DejaVu Sans-like text; qualitative panels add small sans/card text. Tables keep a more consistent size than figures, but full-width assets and wrapfigures compress chart labels.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Yellow–green–blue/purple appears across quantitative charts, and pale yellow/green/blue recurs in qualitative cards. Series semantics are not globally fixed: colors often encode model/source/category locally, with little shape/line redundancy. Tables correctly avoid color, but several chart gradients are decorative and some color mappings are not grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Use a fixed task-category facet grammar so every dose-response panel shares the same x intervention and category labels.
Hold total token volume fixed while isolating source/category proportions, then use a compact recipe table to expose language cost and visual gain together.
Pair quantitative mechanism curves with an isomorphic five-condition qualitative answer strip, and label the strip as illustrative evidence.
Show overall benchmark performance beside structural slices such as object size, while preserving split definitions and weighted aggregate semantics.
failure_patterns: Point estimates dominate; seed dispersion, error bars and confidence definitions are absent.
Visible translucent bands in Figures 2 and 4 have no statistical definition.
Source-order color gradients in Figures 3 and 8 have no explicit semantic legend.
Single-column scaling makes long legends, rotated labels and qualitative answer text difficult to read.
Rank/weighted-Overall rules and multi-label denominators are not fully encoded in tables/captions.
Single qualitative cases in Figures 9, 13 and 14 carry mechanism intuition beyond their statistical scope.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a staged visual chain—task definition, source/scale intervention, calibrated mixture selection, structural diagnosis, encoder/removal check, large-scale validation and appendix failure cases—to argue that reasoning and perception priors have different data origins.
